# layer-nerdctl

nerdctl (the containerd CLI) plus the rootless containerd + buildkit + CNI
stack, as ONE candy. Composed by a box that wants the opt-in `engine: nerdctl`
engine.

## What it installs

- **Native packages** on Arch/CachyOS/Omarchy and Alpine: `nerdctl`, `containerd`,
  `cni-plugins`, `rootlesskit`, `slirp4netns`, `buildkit`, `fuse-overlayfs`,
  `crun`, `iptables-nft` (arch) / `iptables` (alpine), plus `shadow`
  (`newuidmap`/`newgidmap`) and `dbus` (the user `dbus.socket`).
- **Non-native distros** (Fedora/Debian/Ubuntu) install the pinned,
  **fatally** sha256-verified `nerdctl-full` tarball (step
  `nerdctl-full-tarball`), which supplies nerdctl + containerd +
  `containerd-fuse-overlayfs-grpc` + CNI + buildkit + rootlesskit in one archive.
  The helpers come from `shadow-utils` (Fedora) or `uidmap`
  (Debian/Ubuntu); the user bus from `dbus-daemon` or `dbus-user-session`.
- `/etc/nerdctl/nerdctl.toml` with `namespace = "default"` (the ONE spelling
  the programme uses) and `cni_path = "/opt/cni/bin"`. The BuildKit socket is
  deliberately NOT pinned: it is a runtime value resolved through the ONE roots
  resolver (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/charly/buildkitd.sock`).
- The `charly` CNI network conflist at `/etc/cni/net.d/charly.conflist`, and the CNI
  plugins at the ONE `cni_path` the toml declares (`/opt/cni/bin`): Arch's package
  installs there, the nerdctl-full tarball extracts to `/usr/local/libexec/cni`, and
  a step links every real plugin to the declared path (no per-distro `cni_path`).
- The rootless **containerd and buildkit user units**
  (`~/.config/systemd/user/{containerd,buildkit}.service`), written from the
  upstream setuptool templates. `ExecStart` goes through `/usr/bin/env` so one
  unit works for both the `/usr/local/bin` (tarball) and `/usr/bin` (package)
  install locations.
- The **nested-pod posture**: userns-scoped `cap_add: ALL`, `/dev/fuse`,
  `/dev/net/tun`, `unmask=/proc/*`.

## The rootless checklist (CONTAINERD.md §2 and §4)

Every item below is a real plan step with a `check:`; the runtime half is
asserted by the `check-nerdctl-rootless` disposable-VM bed.

| Item | Where | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|
| `newuidmap` / `newgidmap` | distro packages (`shadow`, `uidmap`, `shadow-utils`) | rootlesskit execs them to write the UID/GID map; the setuptool checks only the binaries **it** installs, never these two |
| `user:100000:65536` in `/etc/subuid` and `/etc/subgid` | plan step `rootless-subuid` | the ranges the helpers consume |
| `user@.service.d/delegate.conf` with `Delegate=cpu cpuset io memory pids` | plan step `rootless-delegate-controllers` | memory/cpuset/io limits and `--cpuset-cpus`; a new login picks it up |
| linger | bed, PERFORM (`loginctl enable-linger`) | the user manager and its units must outlive the login session |
| `/dev/fuse` | bed, PRESENCE (opens the node) | the fuse-overlayfs fallback is a libfuse3 client; the setuptool checks the binaries and never the node |
| user D-Bus (`dbus-user-session` / `dbus-daemon` / `dbus`) | package + bed (`dbus.socket`) | the rootless unit has `Requires=dbus.socket` |
| `slirp4netns` as the network driver | the containerd unit sets `CONTAINERD_ROOTLESS_ROOTLESSKIT_NET=slirp4netns` | the documented default |
| the setuptool run | bed, PERFORM (`install` + `install-buildkit`) | starts and enables the written units |
| `namespace = "default"` | `nerdctl.toml` | one namespace spelling, no per-layer name |

### Network drivers — the measured state

- **`slirp4netns` is the default** and is pinned in the unit.
- **`pasta` is an option, not a recommendation.** Measured on rootlesskit 3.3.0
  with pasta `2026_10_02.cba3570`: `rootlesskit --net=pasta true` returns rc 0.
  The deployment's networking properties (published ports bind `0.0.0.0`,
  container→host loopback is blocked, no ephemeral host port) are measured on
  slirp4netns, so pasta is not recommended.
- **`bypass4netns` is an option only where rootlesskit serves it.** The setuptool
  can install `bypass4netnsd`, and nerdctl annotates a container with
  `nerdctl/bypass4netns=true`. Measured on rootlesskit 3.3.0, both
  `--net=bypass4netns` and `--port-driver=bypass4netns` are refused
  (`unknown network mode` / `unknown port driver`), so this layer does not set it.

### Low ports — a documented option, never forced

Do **not** lower `net.ipv4.ip_unprivileged_port_start` for this layer. A rootless
**publish** of a port below 1024 fails `bind: permission denied` until the host
lowers it; the **container-side** threshold is the CNI netns's own `0`, so a
process inside a rootless lease binds a low port with no sysctl at all. If a
specific deploy needs the publish side, set it deliberately in
`/etc/sysctl.d/` on that host — never here, and never as a blanket default.

## Engine capability

The `engine: nerdctl` word is served by `opencharly/plugin-nerdctl`
(out-of-process) or compiled in; every engine op delegates to
`container.InvokeEngineOp("nerdctl", …)` in the spec module. nerdctl has no
`--keep-id`, so the start-plan runs the workload as `--user 0:0` (uid 0 == the
host user under rootless), guaranteeing uid-identical sharing; a non-zero uid
needs the subuid caveat.

## Checks and the R10 bed

- The candy's `check:` steps prove the static half on every distro arm: the
  helpers, the subuid ranges, the delegation drop-in, D-Bus, slirp4netns, the
  written units (marker + `systemd-analyze --user verify`), `namespace =
  "default"`, and a **negative** test that the checksum verifier rejects a
  corrupted archive.
- `check-nerdctl-rootless` (root `charly.yml`, disposable VM) is the runtime
  gate: ABSENCE (no rootless daemon) → PERFORM (daemon-reload, linger, the
  setuptool) → PRESENCE (`nerdctl info` reports `name=rootless`, the helpers
  resolve, `/dev/fuse` opens, the units are active). It records the rootful
  system socket's inode/mtime before the daemon starts and asserts it is
  unchanged after, and that the rootless daemon listens on the user socket.

## Use when

Working with the nerdctl engine, the layer-nerdctl candy, the rootless
containerd/buildkit checklist, or an `engine: nerdctl` deploy.
